races.name: Summer Plate Ladies Day Book Now Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner who should get uncontested lead but showed little promise in recent bumper debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed only a glimmer of promise before weakening into well-held sixth on recent bumper debut at Southwell (good); needs to take a good step forward on this hurdling debut.

runners_data.name: Cockney Cleopatra
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up type with solid RPR of 114 but concerning recent pull-ups for new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten far when fifth of nine in Clonmel maiden (2m, soft) in November but pulled up twice for new stable at Fontwell this spring (2m3f/2m1f); could be considered only if lively in the betting.

runners_data.name: Bailey's Luck
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old making hurdle debut with hood fitted after poor Flat showing
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten when 200-1 for 1m AW maiden on Flat debut in September; now switched to hurdling with a hood fitted.

runners_data.name: Aimeric
runners_data.note: Prominent runner now in visor but was hesitant at flights on disappointing hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Smart on the Flat at his best but signed off for Karl Burke with two disappointing runs in the autumn and was rather hesitant at some of the flights when disappointing favourite on last month's stable/hurdle debut; subsequently tailed off in major Flat handicap; may yet get his act together over hurdles but he is very tricky to weigh up at the moment.

runners_data.name: Wahraan
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up horse with useful form figures but long 131-day absence is a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Has some useful Flat form and kept on steadily from a long way off the pace to take third on hurdle debut at Wetherby (2m, soft) in November; subsequent Grade 2 defeat is easily overlooked but he has become a very awkward ride, often refusing to settle and/or hanging; comes with risk.

runners_data.name: Popalot
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who was well beaten at 40-1 here just 20 days ago over shorter trip
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced in two course bumpers last season but made low-key start to hurdling career when well beaten at 40-1 here (2m) three weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Prince Abu
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 679-day absence with tongue-tie fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced since his two very underwhelming hurdle runs for Derek Shaw in summer 2024 and returned from 318-day absence with 19l defeat off basement Flat mark last month; swaps hood for refitted cheekpieces; tongue-tie a first.

runners_data.name: Jessie Jump Jet
runners_data.note: Patient type who went close last time at Warwick over longer trip with peak form figures
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 over hurdles but went close in Class 5 handicap at Warwick (2m5f, good) this month and should be fine over today's shorter trip; might have been found a good opportunity.

races.paceDynamic: Frisky Whiskey is the only confirmed front runner in this eight-runner maiden hurdle and should get an uncontested lead with the prominent runners Aimeric unlikely to apply serious early pressure. The lack of genuine pace angles means a moderate tempo through the early stages, with hold-up horses like Cockney Cleopatra, Wahraan, and Jessie Jump Jet likely tracking from midfield and beyond. The race will develop into a tactical affair where positioning turning for home becomes crucial, with the winner likely emerging from those who can produce a sustained finish from the back half of the field. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses and patient tactics over front-running or prominent racing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and kick comes late
scenarios.body: The patient runners get perfect positioning and the race becomes a test of who finishes strongest from off the pace. Cockney Cleopatra and Wahraan benefit most from this tactical development.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner controls completely
scenarios.trigger: If Frisky Whiskey gets away with very soft fractions throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to dictate completely and the hold-up horses leave themselves too much to do. Frisky Whiskey benefits from the tactical scenario while Aimeric gets first run from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improver strikes from nowhere
scenarios.trigger: If Bailey's Luck or another unconsidered runner has improved dramatically
scenarios.body: The form horses cancel each other out in a tactical finish and a lightly-raced or returning horse produces unexpected improvement. Bailey's Luck or Prince Abu could surprise if they've come forward significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo becomes crawling and turns into a pure sprint
scenarios.body: The race becomes a dash from the last flight where early pace positioning matters more than running style. Frisky Whiskey and Aimeric benefit from being closer to the pace when the sprint develops.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Frisky Whiskey gets easy early fractions as the only pace angle - could steal race if uncontested
Monitor Cockney Cleopatra's jumping early after two recent pull-ups for new connections
Check if Bailey's Luck shows any early promise on hurdle debut as market may underestimate improvement
Observe Aimeric's confidence at the flights after previous hesitant jumping performance
Watch pace development through first half-mile as moderate tempo will suit patient finishers over front runners

races.name: Geoff Handley's Grand 80th Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Livano Bello
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to fences after disappointing hurdles effort, carries top weight but his style suits the likely tactical pace
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't fire over hurdles at Perth a fortnight ago and is now 0-13 in that sphere but he's generally pretty consistent and will be suited by the trip-and-ground combination on this chasing debut.

runners_data.name: Get A Superstar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 203 days off, needs strong pace to be effective but trainer has decent recent strike-rate
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on chasing debut in December 2024 but raced only once last season, when modest seventh in Sedgefield race won by El Muchacho in November; back from another layoff today; current ability is hard to gauge.

runners_data.name: El Muchacho
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent course form including recent second over course and distance, carried by proven finishing kick
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice on good ground (2m5f/2m3f) for this new stable last season and has been placed on last three appearances, most recently when second over C&D (good) three weeks ago; 1lb lower today and seems very likely to be in the thick of things again.

runners_data.name: Play By The Rules
runners_data.note: Prominent type with promising stable debut last time, significantly lighter weight could prove decisive advantage in small field
runners_data.comment: Shaped well for new yard with Newcastle fifth, then brought down early at Hexham; player
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from long absence with a promising stable debut at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in March, when he travelled strongly for a long way, and he was unlucky to be brought down fairly early on at Hexham this month; remains well handicapped on old form; might be the answer.

races.paceDynamic: Livano Bello will set the early fractions with Play By The Rules likely tracking prominently, creating a modest but sustainable gallop over this stamina-sapping trip. The hold-up horses El Muchacho and Get A Superstar will need the pace to collapse in the final half-mile to be effective. With only four runners and no confirmed pace pressers, this sets up as a tactical affair that will develop late. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can dictate terms and kick when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Control
scenarios.trigger: If Livano Bello and Play By The Rules maintain strong positions throughout the middle stages
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows them to conserve energy before unleashing decisive moves from the front. Hold-up horses face an impossible task trying to reel in well-positioned leaders with tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong and the leaders tire significantly
scenarios.body: El Muchacho's proven course form and finishing kick becomes decisive as the prominently-raced horses pay for their exertions. Get A Superstar could also benefit from the collapse but needs everything to fall right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Livano Bello Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Livano Bello gets an uncontested lead and maintains relentless galloping
scenarios.body: His prominent style perfectly suits the tactical nature and he simply outstays his rivals in a true test of stamina. The lack of pace pressure early allows him to dictate completely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all four runners arrive together turning for home in a slowly-run race
scenarios.body: The finish becomes a pure sprint where fitness and recent form matter most, potentially suiting whichever horse has timed their preparation best. This chaos scenario could throw up any winner.

watchPoints.text: El Muchacho needs the pace to develop strongly early or his hold-up style becomes ineffective in a four-runner tactical affair
Get A Superstar's 203-day absence creates fitness concerns especially given his hold-up style requires sustained finishing effort
Play By The Rules carries 22 pounds less than the top weights which could prove crucial in a stamina test
Livano Bello's recent hurdles form shows concerning trend but his return to chasing over this trip should suit better
The small field size makes early positioning absolutely critical with little room for tactical errors

races.name: Family Extravaganza Raceday On Sunday 5th July Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cher Tara
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid recent form who benefits from the likely strong pace and has proven stamina for this trip on good ground.
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't run badly when fifth of eight at Kelso (2m5f, good) three weeks ago and continues to slip down the weights but has modest 2-21 strike-rate over hurdles; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Lone Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from in-form Kirby yard who won over course and distance previously and showed decent form behind at Kelso last time.
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised upon some considerable help from the handicapper when winning over C&D (good) just under a year ago and returns here after a decent effort at Kelso this month, but she's nothing like the force of old and has become inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Royal Maggs
runners_data.note: Prominent type who fades in the finish and faces concerns about lasting home strongly in what could become a sprint.
runners_data.spotlight: Last of four when upped to 2m7f for last month's handicap debut and only eighth of ten (behind Lone Star) when dropped back to 2m5f at Kelso three weeks ago; not beaten far in either of those races but needs to up her game; usual hood is left off.

runners_data.name: Little Soiree
runners_data.note: Prominent runner now 20lb lower in the weights but has badly lost form and represents a huge leap of faith despite the class drop.
runners_data.spotlight: Now 20lb lower than when winning over 2m for Chris Gordon just over a year ago but has badly lost her way; huge leap of faith is required to support her.

runners_data.name: Mistral Blue
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter with dual 2m3f hurdle wins on good ground who should get an easy lead but needs to prove stamina at this longer trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 2m3f hurdle winner on good ground; pulled up on soft at end of last year but returned from a break with a quite encouraging fifth of 12 at Warwick (2m5f, good) this month and enters calculations here.

runners_data.name: Time Was
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 93-day break who has been consistent in the frame recently and gets excellent conditions for patient tactics.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-19 under rules but returned from a break with a clear second over C&D (good to soft) in November and made the frame on all three subsequent appearances; returns from another break today; can make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Parish Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 2-5 record for new stable this year who coped well with good ground when third at Kelso and suits the likely race shape.
runners_data.spotlight: 2-5 for new stable this year; gained the wins on heavy and good to soft ground but coped perfectly well with good ground when close third at Kelso (2m5f; first-time tongue-tie) last month; hood (worn for three of her last four races) is discarded; likely contender again.

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from long break with wind surgery and first-time hood who needs to prove both fitness and ability.
runners_data.spotlight: Unplaced all six hurdle runs, most recently when pulled up in soft-ground handicap on stable debut in January; combination of wind surgery, first-time hood and return to good ground could plausibly prompt a better performance here, though; worth a glance in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Mistral Blue is the only confirmed front-runner and will dictate proceedings from the start, likely establishing a sustainable gallop without pressure from the prominent runners Lone Star, Royal Maggs and Little Soiree. The modest early pace will see the hold-up horses Cher Tara, Time Was, Parish Star and Lady Fortune tracking in behind, setting up a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs. With no genuine pace pressure early, this race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can produce their best work late when the tempo lifts. The lack of early burn-up creates ideal conditions for patient tactics and late-closing runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue sets steady fractions and the race becomes a sprint from 3f out
scenarios.body: The patient riders can time their challenges perfectly as the early leaders tire, with the genuine staying power telling in the final furlong. Hold-up specialists get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent horse capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can track the leader and kick clear before the hold-up horses get organised
scenarios.body: Lone Star or Royal Maggs could steal a march by moving into contention 4f out, gaining vital momentum before the closers respond. The winner gets first run and holds on grimly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals it
scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue gets very soft fractions early and has enough left for a sustained kick
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to conserve energy perfectly, then quicken clear when the field comes to challenge 3f out. The prominent trackers struggle to respond to the change of pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is pedestrian and no horse can inject genuine pace until too late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy scramble with horses getting in each other's way, favouring those with tactical speed who can find gaps. Positioning luck becomes crucial in a slowly-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Mistral Blue must be watched for signs of stopping if the pace quickens significantly from 4f out as stamina questions remain at this trip.
Royal Maggs tends to fade in the finish so watch for her dropping away tamely if the race becomes a genuine test of stamina.
Time Was returns from a 93-day break so monitor for any signs of needing the run despite her consistent recent form when fresh.
Little Soiree has badly lost her way recently so watch for early signs of whether the weight drop has rekindled any spark.
Parish Star's ability to handle the likely sprint finish will be crucial given her hold-up style and need to weave through traffic.

races.name: Anji Fletcher Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Snatch A Glance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner suited by the lack of early pace, fresh after 36 days and Fern O'Brien's 5lb claim helpful in handicap context
runners_data.spotlight: Just did enough to win 2m Ludlow maiden in the autumn and was a very respectable third of six in novice event over that C&D (again on good) last month; moves up in trip for handicap debut; should have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer well below his prime but Harry Cobden booking and cheekpieces added last time suggest connections still have hope
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful hurdler/chaser in his prime; well below best during a fairly light campaign last season (four hurdle runs; cheekpieces added last time) but will appreciate this ease in grade and has slipped to a dangerous mark.

runners_data.name: Jackstell
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can control this small field but 178-day absence is a concern despite three autumn wins showing his best form
runners_data.spotlight: Won three consecutive small-field races in the autumn, the latest a Plumpton handicap (2m4f, good); absent since struggling on soft ground there in December but remains lightly raced and could plausibly still have more improvement to come.

runners_data.name: High Dancer
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the race shape perfectly and good recent form on similar trips, though cheekpieces suggest he needs encouragement
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't see out 3m when well-held third at Doncaster (good to soft) in March but ran well for a long way and is now back on same mark as for his clear second behind a useful rival there (2m3f, soft) in November; also suited by good ground; could be a tough nut to crack if aided by new cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Sun Art
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs the pace to develop but Jack Hogan's 3lb claim and good recent Hereford second keeps him competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any further progress since winning a 2m Ludlow novice in March 2025 but posted a sound effort when second off today's mark at Hereford (2m, good) last month and is work another crack at this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Nitty Gritty
runners_data.note: Another hold-up performer racing in cheekpieces, freshest in the field at 12 days but poor stable record creates doubts
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 for current stable (since the autumn) and has a very mixed record but ran well when second in refitted cheekpieces at Kelso (2m5f, good) this month and was unlucky to come to grief at Uttoxeter recently; remains on a good mark; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Lord Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Talented hold-up horse whose 12-length Hereford win was impressive but needs this race to unfold tactically to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed considerable improvement when winning easily by 12l on last month's handicap hurdle debut at Hereford (2m, good); managed only third under 7lb penalty here (2m2f, good) eight days later and is another 5lb higher today, but he moves up in trip again and remains of interest.

races.paceDynamic: Jackstell will take the field along from the front with Snatch A Glance and High Dancer tracking prominently in second and third. With only one confirmed pace-setter in a small field of seven, Jackstell can dictate proceedings without pressure and build a sustainable rhythm over this extended 2m4½f trip. The lack of early pace pressure means the race will likely develop into a tactical affair where horses need to be handy turning for home. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical pace who can position close to Jackstell rather than hold-up horses who will struggle to make up ground from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackstell Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Jackstell gets an uncontested lead and maintains his recent winning form
scenarios.body: His three consecutive autumn wins show he thrives when allowed to dictate, and after 178 days off he should be fresh enough to see out the trip. The lack of early pressure plays directly into his hands with Gavin Sheehan able to control the tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Snatch A Glance or High Dancer can track Jackstell and outfinish him up the hill
scenarios.body: Both have shown good form on similar going recently and can sit in the perfect stalking position behind the leader. Their fresher profiles compared to Jackstell's long absence could prove decisive in a finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and the race falls apart in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Sun Art and Lord Chamberlain have the class to pick up the pieces if the prominent runners tie up. Lord Chamberlain's 12-length Hereford win shows he has a devastating turn of foot when things fall right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a tactical crawl and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Nitty Gritty's recent second at Kelso in cheekpieces or Crebilly finding some spark from his prime form could capitalise. The light weights and tactical nature could suit an unconsidered runner.

watchPoints.text: Jackstell's jumping under pressure after 178 days off - any mistakes could hand the initiative to the trackers
Lord Chamberlain's tongue-tie first time - if it improves his breathing he could be much better than his odds suggest
High Dancer's cheekpieces and how aggressively Danny McMenamin rides him early - needs to be handy in this small field
The pace through the middle section - if Jackstell goes too slow it becomes a sprint which favours the classier hold-up horses
Sun Art and how quickly Jack Hogan can get him into contention - his best form comes when not too far back early

races.name: Dine In The Altior's Resturant Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Front-runner with confirmed tactical advantage, 44 days since last run but won over course and distance in good form
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who was left clear just after final fence to score over C&D (good) last month, opening his chase account at the 12th attempt; evidently in good nick and subsequent 4lb rise is not excessive.

runners_data.name: Lheur De Gloire
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who shaped well before fading last time, first run after wind operation but quick return
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles but shaped well before fading into fourth of 13 at Southwell (2m, good; first run after wind op) this month and Ben Pauling is evidently keen to launch his chasing career; interesting.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, good recent course form but 0-6 over fences and poor effort at Stratford last time
runners_data.spotlight: Not at his best at Stratford 11 days ago and now 0-6 over fences but he had returned from a break with a pretty good third over C&D (good) last month and his current mark is workable.

runners_data.name: Walk The Plank
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 71-day break, narrow chase winner in March but modest form level
runners_data.spotlight: Battled well for narrow success at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March, his third start over fences; that form looks modest and he's 4lb higher here but further progress is possible.

runners_data.name: Intenzo
runners_data.note: Prominent early style but three poor efforts since promising chase debut, inexperienced 3lb claimer aboard
runners_data.spotlight: Made a promising chase/handicap debut when clear second at Sedgefield (2m, good; form well advertised by winner since) in March but three lesser efforts have followed and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry.

races.paceDynamic: Catchim will lead from the start with his confirmed front-running style, setting a sustainable pace without pressure from the predominantly hold-up field. Intenzo may take a prominent early position but the remainder - Lheur De Gloire, Cawthorne Cracker and Walk The Plank - are all hold-up performers who will sit back and wait. With minimal early pace pressure, Catchim can dictate terms and control the gallop throughout the 2m1f trip. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner Catchim, who can utilise his tactical advantage to build an unassailable lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Catchim Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Catchim gets an easy lead and maintains a steady gallop to the home turn.
scenarios.body: He can kick clear after the final fence as he did when winning here last month, with the hold-up horses left with too much ground to make up. His front-running style is perfectly suited to dominate this weak pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Catches Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their challenges perfectly and Catchim weakens in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Walk The Plank or Lheur De Gloire could produce strong finishes to overhaul a tiring leader, particularly if the pace has been genuine enough to stretch Catchim's stamina. The 8-year-old Catchim may be vulnerable late after making all the running.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Intenzo Pressures Early
scenarios.trigger: If Intenzo takes a more aggressive approach and challenges Catchim for the early lead.
scenarios.body: This creates a faster pace that could set up the race for the deeper closers like Cawthorne Cracker, though Intenzo's recent poor form makes this scenario less likely. The increased gallop would compromise both early leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Jumping Disrupts
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make jumping errors at crucial stages, particularly the inexperienced chasers.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble where any horse left with a clear round could capitalise, though Catchim's experience over fences gives him the edge even in chaotic circumstances. Poor jumping would particularly affect the hold-up horses trying to make late progress.

watchPoints.text: Catchim must be watched for early sharpness after 44-day layoff, any sluggish jumping could compromise his front-running advantage
Lheur De Gloire for signs of fitness following wind operation, any laboured breathing or early struggles indicate the procedure hasn't worked
Walk The Plank for ring rustiness after 71-day absence, particularly his jumping rhythm in the early stages
Charlie Maggs on Intenzo for any positive trainer instructions given recent poor form, watch if he takes Intenzo forward early
The pace through the first mile for sustainability, if Catchim goes too fast early the hold-up horses come into play

races.name: Half Year Annual Badges On Sale Now Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Iolaos Du Mou
runners_data.spotlight: Just held on to make all at Warwick in this month last year and returned from layoff with encouraging sixth of 16 at Uttoxeter 26 days ago, weakening out of contention in only the closing stages; no surprise if he gives this a good shot.

runners_data.name: Ruler Legend
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent recent course form and proven ability on good ground at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season in excellent form, winning twice here (2m/2m2f) on good ground, and is probably still on a workable mark; big chance.

runners_data.name: Assorda
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who needs a strong pace to be effective, struggling since her fortunate Catterick win
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French mare; fortunate to win small-field Catterick novice (1m7f, good) for Paula Smith on British debut in March 2025 and soundly beaten in all five subsequent handicaps, the last four times for new stable this year; drops back in trip (from 2m4f).

runners_data.name: Bunker Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up type carrying bottom weight with breathing issues last time, but showed clear second form to Ruler Legend here
runners_data.spotlight: Reportedly had breathing issue when well beaten at Perth last month and is now 0-9 over hurdles but his clear second to next-time-out winner Ruler Legend over C&D (good) two starts ago was a good effort; big player if back at that level.

runners_data.name: Paragon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making only his fifth hurdles start, showed encouragement in handicap debut at Southwell
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 on the Flat and 0-4 over hurdles; made a fairly encouraging handicap hurdle debut when sixth of 13 at Southwell (2m, good) this month, though, and might be boosted by refitted cheekpieces here.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong trainer form (5/20) who finished well for third over course and distance on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer; yet to make a significant impact over hurdles but was given a lot to do before finishing well for third over C&D (good) on handicap debut three weeks ago, and his recent Flat run was perfectly respectable.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 342-day absence, placed in this race at 80-1 last year but hard to recommend
runners_data.spotlight: Belied 80-1 odds when placed off today's mark in this race last year but was well beaten on next hurdling start and has been absent since some disappointing Flat runs in the autumn; too risky.

runners_data.name: Melosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who was pulled up on hurdles debut here over longer trip, dropping back in distance today
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability on the Flat but was pulled up when 100-1 for handicap hurdle debut here (2m4f, good) in April; drops back in trip today; can't be recommended.

races.paceDynamic: Iolaos Du Mou is listed as a non-runner but was the only confirmed front-runner, leaving this race without a natural pace-setter. Ruler Legend and Paragon both show prominent tendencies and will likely dispute the early lead, creating a moderate tempo over this testing 2m½f trip. The majority of the field comprises hold-up horses (Assorda, Bunker Bay, Made All, Red Trail, Melosa) who will be looking to come from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can secure good early positions without the pressure of a genuine speed horse, as the hold-up brigade will struggle to make up ground in a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ruler Legend Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Legend secures an uncontested lead and dictates a steady pace
scenarios.body: His proven course form and current ratings edge give him every chance to kick clear when the pace lifts. The lack of early pressure allows him to save energy for a strong finish over his favoured trip and surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Paragon Presses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Paragon shows more early speed than expected and pressures the pace
scenarios.body: This creates a stronger gallop that could set up the race for the hold-up horses to close from the back. Made All and Assorda would benefit most from this increased tempo over the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If neither Ruler Legend nor Paragon establishes clear control early
scenarios.body: The race becomes stop-start with multiple horses vying for position, favouring those with tactical speed. Bunker Bay's second to Ruler Legend here previously suggests he can capitalise on a muddled pace scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Late Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the early stages
scenarios.body: This sets up a sprint finish where class tells, but the lack of early pace makes it difficult for hold-up horses to make up significant ground. The prominent runners still hold the tactical advantage even in a slowly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Iolaos Du Mou confirmed as non-runner despite being listed, removing the only genuine front-runner from this contest
Bunker Bay reportedly had breathing issues at Perth and now wears a tongue-strap, monitor early market moves for confidence
Red Trail returning from 342-day layoff with disappointing recent Flat form, needs to show significant improvement
Made All represents the in-form Sam England stable (5/20 recent record) and finished strongly over course and distance last time
Paragon dropping to bottom end of weights at 157lbs and could improve significantly on his encouraging Southwell effort
